baseline.design: compact bootstrap with every provenance source URL embedded

alternatives.description: Remove provenance from the bootstrap entirely and expose full provenance only from the selected identity's existing content-addressed detail record.
alternatives.runtime_tradeoff: Smallest payload, but the focus view would have no source fallback when the catalog platform or selected detail is unavailable.

alternatives.description: Embed exactly one URL-only provenance source per project, retain activity.observed_at only for unknown-status notices, and upgrade the selected focus view to full canonical provenance only after existing generation-, byte- and SHA-256-bound detail verification.
alternatives.runtime_tradeoff: Costs 701 gzip bytes versus zero-provenance, but preserves one meaningful source during catalog-platform degradation and requires no new request class or backend.

selection_reason: The selected hybrid clears the task's 2048-byte warning-headroom target while preserving a degraded-mode evidence link. It reuses the already deployed content-addressed selected-detail fetch instead of adding startup requests, segmented bootstrap fetches, a backend, or a second catalog truth.

runtime_memory.policy: The selected-detail Promise cache and decoded verified full-record retention are both capped at one identity; changing focus evicts the prior detail promise/result, while compact shard transport remains separately bounded to eight.
runtime_memory.reason: Fulfilled detail promises retain decoded records, so both retention layers must share the one-identity bound rather than allowing hidden accumulation.

does_not_establish: that zero-provenance is unsafe in every future design
permission to remove the DE/EN no-JavaScript recovery path
future performance after additional catalog growth

review_fixes.codex_p1: canonical state now authorizes only verified selected provenance.sources while full runtime catalogue cutover remains false
review_fixes.codex_p2: fulfilled detail promises can retain decoded records, so CATALOG_DETAIL_CACHE_LIMIT and both cache contracts are now one; browser eviction cycle proves reload after another identity
